title: Finite maps of strict affinoids induce finite maps on canonical reductions
statement: Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], complete for a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value. Let $A,B\ne0$ be reduced strict affinoid $K$-algebras: each is a quotient of a restricted-series ring $K\langle T_1,\ldots,T_r\rangle$ [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation], with its affinoid Banach topology. For $H=A,B$ put $\rho_H(h)=\sup_\chi|\chi(h)|$, with $\chi:H\to K$ ranging over continuous unital $K$-algebra homomorphisms, and put $H_{\le1}=\{h:\rho_H(h)\le1\}$, $H_{<1}=\{h:\rho_H(h)<1\}$ and $\widetilde H=H_{\le1}/H_{<1}$. Write $\kappa=\{a\in K:|a|\le1\}/\{a\in K:|a|<1\}$. If a unital $K$-algebra homomorphism $\varphi:A\to B$ makes $B$ a finitely generated $A$-module, then $\varphi$ is continuous, $\rho_B(\varphi(a))\le\rho_A(a)$ for all $a\in A$, and the induced $\kappa$-algebra homomorphism $\widetilde\varphi:\widetilde A\to\widetilde B$ makes $\widetilde B$ a finitely generated $\widetilde A$-module. Neither injectivity of $\varphi$ nor surjectivity on reductions is assumed.

source.place: BGR Theorem 6.3.5/1, finite map implies finite reduction map. Independently read in Temkin, A new proof of the Gerritzen-Grauert theorem, introduction printed p.2 and section 2 (definition of reduction); https://math.huji.ac.il/~temkin/papers/Gerritzen_Grauert.pdf. BGR archival copy WANTED; source is not locally present.

proof.text: For $H=A,B$, compare the character supremum in the statement with the maximal-ideal supremum of [lem-trf-affinoid-supremum-seminorm-calculus]. Each maximal residue field $H/\mathfrak m$ is finite over $K$. It equals $K$: every residue element satisfies a polynomial over $K$ by linear dependence of its powers, and factoring that polynomial over the algebraically closed field forces the element to be a scalar. The residue map $\chi_{\mathfrak m}:H\to K$ is continuous, since the cited inequality gives $|\chi_{\mathfrak m}(h)|\le\|h\|_q$ for a Tate quotient norm. Conversely, each unital $K$-algebra character onto $K$ has maximal kernel and is this residue map. Thus the two suprema agree, including before continuity of $\varphi$ is known.

source.place: Section 1.4, Propositions 6 and 8, printed pp.24-25; character comparison over an algebraically closed base written out here. Primary PDF read online 2026-10-24; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: The arbitrary-homomorphism inequality of [lem-trf-affinoid-supremum-seminorm-calculus], together with step 1, gives $\rho_B(\varphi(a))\le\rho_A(a)$. Apply [lem-trf-affinoid-spectral-banach-norm] to the two nonzero reduced strict affinoids. For quotient norms choose its constant $M_B$ on $B$. Then $\|\varphi(a)-\varphi(a\prime)\|_{B,q}\le M_B\rho_B(\varphi(a-a\prime))\le M_B\rho_A(a-a\prime)\le M_B\|a-a\prime\|_{A,q}$. This Lipschitz inequality proves continuity for their affinoid topologies.

source.place: Theorem 1.2.6(1),(5), printed pp.6-7, and the following paragraph; the continuity deduction is the displayed inequality. Primary PDF read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: The nonarchimedean norm inequalities of step 2 show that $H_{\le1}$ is a subring and $H_{<1}$ an ideal in it: $\rho_H(xy)\le\rho_H(x)\rho_H(y)$ and $\rho_H(x+y)\le\max(\rho_H(x),\rho_H(y))$. Also $\rho_H(c\cdot1)=|c|$, so the scalar map takes $V=\{c:|c|\le1\}$ into $H_{\le1}$ and $\mathfrak m_V=\{c:|c|<1\}$ into $H_{<1}$. The contraction in step 2 maps both these subrings and ideals for $A$ into the corresponding ones for $B$. Hence $[a]\mapsto[\varphi(a)]$ is well defined on the quotients and fixes the residue scalars $\kappa=V/\mathfrak m_V$. This constructs the stated $\kappa$-algebra map.

source.place: Section 2, definition of reduction; quotient-ring verification written out here. Primary PDF read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Extend $\widetilde H$ to any nonzero algebraic Tate quotient using the maximal-ideal supremum in [lem-trf-affinoid-supremum-seminorm-calculus]. At every maximal ideal the extending absolute value gives $|x+y|\le\max(|x|,|y|)$, $|xy|\le|x||y|$ and $|c\cdot1|=|c|$. Taking suprema gives the same inequalities for $\rho_H$, so $H_{\le1}$ is a subring, $H_{<1}$ is an ideal in it, and scalars induce the residue-field action. Nonemptiness of the maximal spectrum follows from [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal] applied to the proper zero ideal. Thus this construction needs no completeness assertion about a quotient norm. For a finite map $\psi:D\to H$, arbitrary-homomorphism contraction induces $\widetilde\psi$ on these quotients. For $h\in H_{\le1}$, [lem-trf-finite-affinoid-spectral-equation] supplies $h^r+\sum_{i=1}^r\psi(d_i)h^{r-i}=0$ with $\rho_D(d_i)^{1/i}\le\rho_H(h)\le1$. Each $d_i$ is in $D_{\le1}$, so reducing this monic equation makes $\bar h$ integral over $\widetilde D$. For $A,B$ this notation agrees with the character construction by step 1.

proof.text: First take a nonzero affinoid DOMAIN $C$. Present it as $T_r/I$. The lift in [lem-trf-tate-normalization-lift] supplies a finite injection $T_d\hookrightarrow C$. Put $R=\kappa[U_1,\ldots,U_d]$ and $S=\widetilde C$. By [lem-trf-tate-spectral-generic-reduction-rank], $R\hookrightarrow S$ is injective, $S$ is reduced and $R$-torsion-free, and its localization at $R\setminus0$ has finite dimension. Step 4 for $T_d\to C$ says $S$ is integral over the reduction of $T_d$, identified with $R$ by coefficient reduction in that cited rank lemma. Thus [lem-trf-integral-generic-finite-algebra] makes $S$ finite over $R$. The variables of $R$ and a finite module-spanning family of $S$ generate $S$ as a $\kappa$-algebra. Hence every such domain has finite-type reduction. This establishes the Tate-normalization case before using any assertion for general finite reduction maps.

source.place: Agent-written reduction-level assembly from Section 1.4 Lemmas 12 and 13 and Noether normalization 1.2 Corollary 10; algebraic finiteness components from the cited Stacks nodes. No use of BGR 6.4.1.

proof.text: Now take any nonzero reduced affinoid $C=T_r/I$. Apply [lem-trf-tate-submodule-norm-controlled-generators] with $D=T_r$ and $s=1$ to every ideal of $T_r$: its finite module generators are ideal generators. Thus $T_r$ is Noetherian; mapping generators of inverse-image ideals proves that its quotient $C$ is Noetherian. Its minimal primes $\mathfrak p_1,\ldots,\mathfrak p_s$ are finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-minimal-primes]. Every prime contains a minimal prime by [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime]. Put $C_i=C/\mathfrak p_i$. Each is a nonzero affinoid domain, presented by the composite $T_r\to C\to C_i$. The quotient map is finite: $1$ generates $C_i$ as a $C$-module. Maximal ideals of $C_i$ correspond to maximal ideals of $C$ containing $\mathfrak p_i$, with identical residue fields. Every maximal ideal of $C$ occurs for at least one $i$. Hence $\rho_{C_i}(c_i)\le\rho_C(c)$ for every $i$; conversely each maximal-residue value of $c$ is at most $\max_i\rho_{C_i}(c_i)$. Taking its supremum proves $\rho_C(c)=\max_i\rho_{C_i}(c_i)$. It follows that the map $\widetilde C\to P:=\prod_i\widetilde C_i$ is injective: a representative mapping to zero has all the finitely many component norms strictly less than one, hence their maximum strictly less than one. The index set is nonempty because a nonzero ring has a maximal ideal, by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal] applied to the proper zero ideal.

proof.text: Each $\widetilde C_i$ is finite type over $\kappa$ by step 5, so $P$ is generated as a $\kappa$-algebra by its finitely many coordinate idempotents and the coordinate-supported finite generating families. Step 4 applies to the finite quotients $C\to C_i$. Consequently every $x=(x_i)\in P$ is integral over $\widetilde C$: choose monic equations $f_i(x_i)=0$ over $\widetilde C$ and use $\prod_i f_i$, whose evaluation has a zero factor in each coordinate. In particular the displayed finite $\kappa$-algebra generators are integral over $\widetilde C$ and also generate $P$ over $\widetilde C$. By [lem-sc-finite-generated-integral-subring], $P$ is finite over $\widetilde C$. The field $\kappa$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are zero and itself). Apply [lem-sfb-artin-tate-subalgebra-finite-type] to the injection of step 6 and this finite extension. It gives that $\widetilde C$ is finite type over $\kappa$. This independently proves the general finite-type fact; it does not cite the descendant node for that fact.

proof.text: Apply step 7 to $C=B$ and choose $\kappa$-algebra generators $\bar b_1,\ldots,\bar b_m$ of $\widetilde B$. Since $\widetilde\varphi$ fixes $\kappa$, these are also $\widetilde A$-algebra generators. Step 4 for the given finite map $A\to B$ makes each of them integral over $\widetilde A$. Thus [lem-sc-finite-generated-integral-subring] says their $\widetilde A$-subalgebra, which is all of $\widetilde B$, is a finite $\widetilde A$-module. Together with steps 1-3 this gives every clause of the unchanged statement. No injection of $A$ into $B$, nor surjection of reductions, was used.
